bean_snapshot.name: Tanzania Peaberry
bean_snapshot.notes: Altitude range 1100–1700 masl. Harvest window May–December 2026.

intent: first roast of a new bean - establish a baseline for Tanzania Peaberry

adjustments.reason: full caramelization aroma, full cinnamon color, silverskin beginning to peel

sensory.aroma_drying: toasted bread at 2:30, beans still green; toasted bread again at 5:00 as color started to change
sensory.aroma_maillard: lightly roasted peanuts at 7:00; caramel malt at 8:30; full caramelization at 10:00
sensory.aroma_development: full roast smell at 15:00 as first crack began
sensory.color_at_yellowing: browning/yellowing at 7:00 with beans plumping; dark popcorn kernel color at 8:30; full cinnamon at 10:00
sensory.color_at_drop: notably dark - darker than the 12.8% weight loss and 60s development would predict
sensory.crack_character: first crack onset 15:00, end 19:00 - 4:00 of crack
sensory.observations: Timer counted down from 18:00; elapsed times derived as 18:00 minus remaining, so notes logged past 0:00 (-1:00, -2:00) are 19:00 and 20:00 elapsed. Silverskin began peeling at 10:00 and was peeling again at 19:00. Dropped to cooldown at 20:00, cooling ran to 26:00 elapsed (6 min). Green weight 250.95g is marginally over the CB-101's 250g rated capacity. Post-roast assessment: color came out considerably darker than target and the cooled beans carry a faint smoke note, despite weight loss (12.8%) and development time (60s) both landing in the light-roast band and no second crack. roast_level_achieved recorded as light on the strength of the moisture and development numbers; the dark surface color reads as a bake artifact from the 20:00 total time rather than a genuinely darker roast. Pending visual check for tipped beans to rule out scorch.

cuppings.brew_method: cupping bowl - 8g coarse, 150mL at 93C, 4 min, crust broken at 4:00
cuppings.aroma_dry: dark chocolate, earth - darker descriptors than a 12.8% weight loss / 60s development roast should produce
cuppings.aroma_wet: smoky and roasty; smoke carried through from the cooled-bean aroma and dominated the crust break

acidity.notes: present and pleasant, more fruity than citric, a touch thin

sweetness.notes: noticeable fruit sweetness; survived despite the long roast

cuppings.finish_quality: lingers a few seconds then disappears; mildly astringent but not unpleasant
cuppings.tasting_notes_free: Better than the roast log predicted. The 20:00 total time and dark surface color suggested a bake, but acidity (3) and sweetness (3) both came through with fruit character intact - the Maillard phase held momentum (ratio 0.40, aroma progressed bready -> peanut -> caramel with no stall), so the bake hypothesis is rejected. The real faults are surface over-roast (smoke and roasty/earthy notes masking the washed Tanzanian citrus character) and mild astringency from the 60s development. Visual check confirmed no tipping, ruling out scorch: the dark surface is prolonged drum contact across 20 minutes, not heat spotting.
cuppings.hypothesis_result: No hypothesis was set - this was a baseline first roast of the bean. Baseline established: 215C charge, 250.95g, 20:00 total, DTR 0.05 yields a drinkable 8/10 cup with fruit and medium body, undercut by smoke and a mildly astringent finish.
cuppings.next_adjustment: Target a medium roast. Drop green weight to 225g (250.95g was over the CB-101's 250g rating and contributed to the 20:00 total) and raise initial temp to 225C. Target first crack onset at 11:00-12:00 and drop at 14:30 for a DTR of ~0.17, up from 0.05. Pre-set the step to 235C at 8:00 on the clock rather than reacting to the aroma cue - temperature steps have landed later than intended on the last two roasts due to countdown-timer math.
